claims.text: DFT calculations can screen and predict alloy compositions that favor stable, protective oxide layers.
DFT-guided alloy design will enhance oxidation resistance under high-temperature conditions.
High-entropy or refractory alloy surfaces can be inherently susceptible to oxidation in high-temperature or oxidative environments.
DFT screening can evaluate energy barriers associated with potential oxide phases on alloy compositions.
DFT screening can evaluate the stability of potential oxide phases on alloy compositions.
Oxide-layer formation governs material degradation under high-temperature oxidation or corrosive atmospheric conditions.
DFT can predict alloy compositions that form coherent, dense, low-energy oxide scales.
Stable oxide layers act as passivating barriers.
Passivating oxide layers slow oxygen diffusion and prevent further oxidation.
DFT can identify alloy compositions that promote protective oxide-scale formation.
Formation of protective oxide scales reduces overall oxidation kinetics.
DFT-selected alloys will exhibit significantly lower oxidation rates than baseline alloys.
Conventional alloys developed without DFT optimization typically have higher oxidation rates and less protective oxide scales.
The effectiveness of DFT-guided optimization is expected to be most pronounced at high temperatures.
Stress-induced oxide spallation and competing oxide phases may reduce the oxidation resistance predicted from oxide stability alone.
